summary.intent: Triage and resolve code-review findings on several stacked PRs (#181/#384 pipe-in-literal projection, #176/#379 local-interface scoping), and research whether oxc's tsrs type checker and a construct-by-construct matrix can help fix silent wrong-type defects in the caliper prop-type extractor.
summary.outcome: Findings were confirmed valid and handed to workers (fixes for #384 and #379 still in progress); Batch 1 of resolver defects landed as draft PR #385 with passing local tests; the construct matrix was produced, and the tsrs analysis was sent back to the worker after it wrongly reported that oxc has no type checker.

repo: Fixes for PR #384 and #379 are being done by workers on the same branches; review findings cannot be marked resolved by the agent. A clean re-review on the new commit clears them, and invalid findings need a user-run dismissal command because dismissals are denied for the agent.

Scope-passing code in the resolver has had two review rounds. The invariant is that a declaration body must be resolved under that declaration's own scope, not the reference site's, and cycle detection should key on the resolved declaration, not just file, name and args.
The evaluator has roughly 26 scope-less call sites, which docs/edge-cases.md already lists as a known gap in #379.

Storybook's proptypes converter splits a raw type name on every `|` and JSON-parses each piece, so string literals containing `|`, `"` or `\` break the raw-name boolean-union form and degrade the control to `object`.
The direct path keeps `Omit<Base,'x'>` and `Pick` as wrappers around the full base without filtering keys; alias paths in #385 now match that.
CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION was not bumped in #385 because the serialized shape is unchanged; the claim that the build fingerprint covers extractor-only changes is unverified.
The stack is #379 <- #385 (Batch 1, trail #255), so #385 must be rebased after #379 settles. The two touch overlapping resolver files.

oxc has no type checker of its own: oxc_semantic provides per-file scopes and symbols, oxc_isolated_declarations only copies or infers obvious annotations, and type-aware linting spawns the external tsgolint (Go), the same architecture as crates/tsc-client. oxc-project/tsrs is a separate repo containing a Rust port of the TS7 checker.

code.finding: Review finding location: the raw-name fallback for boolean unions breaks literals containing `|`.
Raw-name fallback for unions with a boolean member.
The addon forwards the raw type name unchanged to Storybook's converter.
On main 644df655, Partial/Required/Omit/Pick aliases were forwarded to their base type (silent wrong type); #385 fixes this.
Tuple optional elements and labels are dropped, and a rest element becomes a double array (line 1006); PropType::Tuple cannot represent them.
Getter members become function fields because the signature kind is ignored, and overloads become two fields.
A mapped type's `as` clause and `readonly` modifier are not read.

workflow: Check upstream sources properly before claiming a tool does not exist; the user caught the agent answering from memory after checking only local copies.
For recurring review findings, enumerate entry points and build a test table by entry point against scenario, and state the invariant with its single enforcement point, before implementing.
Require failing-first tests on real source, and prove nothing else moved with unchanged snapshots and a byte-identical output check against main.

Subagent briefs can carry wrong facts (the 'TS does not reduce literal | string' claim was wrong) and workers can miss later corrections, so re-send corrections and have workers verify against the real checker.

friction: The agent's initial answer that oxc has no type checker was wrong, caused by shallow lookup; the user had to correct it.
The construct-matrix worker went idle still saying 'oxc has no type checker' because it never saw the correction, so the tsrs analysis had to be re-requested.
The brief said TS does not reduce `'a'|'b'|string`, which is false; the worker corrected it.
The #176 change showed 4 open findings, not the 3 the user mentioned.
The worker's checkout was 56 files behind main, so line numbers differ between its report and the working branch.
Performance evidence for #385 is thin: only the small fixtures/chakra fixture was used, because Mantine is not installed and corpora are not to be fetched.
Entire Gates on #385 was still pending, and some snapshot tests fail in the worker's worktree on environment issues.
